results.name: Oligo Security Raises $60 Million, Valuation Doubles
results.content:
Israeli cybersecurity company [Oligo Security](https://www.linkedin.com/company/oligo-security/) has secured $60 million in a new funding round after reporting sharp revenue growth and a doubling of its valuation since its Series B financing.  
The round was backed by Ballistic Ventures, Greenfield Partners, Red Dot Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners and TLV Partners. Investors Yasmin Lukatz and Eyal Waldman also participated. The latest investment takes Oligo’s total funding since its launch in 2022 to approximately $140 million.  
The company plans to use the capital to speed up product innovation and strengthen its presence in markets outside Israel. The fundraising follows a period in which Oligo said its annual recurring revenue increased by more than 300% year over year, alongside an expansion of its operations.
#### Research brings Oligo Security wider attention  
Alongside its commercial expansion, Oligo has gained visibility through cybersecurity research involving AI infrastructure and widely used web browsers.  
In May 2024, its researchers uncovered an attack affecting thousands of servers used to train and operate AI systems. The servers had reportedly been compromised through a vulnerability that existing security tools had failed to detect.  
About two months later, the company identified another security issue affecting major browsers, including Chrome, Safari and Firefox. The weakness could allow a malicious website to bypass security protections and reach services running on a user’s computer or home network.  
Those services would normally be accessible only from within the device or local network. Browser developers subsequently updated their security mechanisms and moved to block the attack method.  
The discoveries helped reinforce Oligo’s argument that many serious threats become visible only when software is observed during actual use.
#### Founded by three childhood friends  
Oligo was established in 2022 by three childhood friends: CEO [Nadav Czerninski,](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nadav-czerninski) [CTO Gal Elbaz](https://www.linkedin.com/in/gal-elbaz/) and [CPO Avshalom Hilu.](https://www.linkedin.com/in/avshalom-hilu/)  
The founders previously served in Israeli military cyber and technology units, including Units 81 and 8200 in Military Intelligence and Matzgov in the C4I Corps.  
The company currently employs about 100 people. Around 70 work at its development centre in Israel, while the remaining employees are based at its offices in New York and San Francisco.  
With new funding in place, Oligo is preparing to expand its technology and international reach while continuing to build around runtime protection. Its next stage of growth will centre on converting its recent revenue momentum and research profile into a broader position in the global application security market.

results.name: Oligo Raises $60 Million for Runtime Security - SecurityWeek
results.content:
**Runtime security company Oligo Security today announced raising $60 million in a new funding round that brings the total to $140 million.**  
Ballistic Ventures, Canon Capital, Greenfield Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Red Dot Capital, TLV Partners, and angel investors participated in the round.  
Founded in 2022, Tel Aviv-based [Oligo](https://www.oligo.security/) has built a security platform covering application code, cloud workloads, and AI systems that provides deep runtime visibility and real-time protection.  
Through code execution observability, the platform enables organizations to block exploit attempts, prioritize risky vulnerabilities, and automate response.  
As the window between vulnerability disclosure and exploitation has diminished significantly in the AI era, Oligo bets on runtime protection to catch exploits at the application layer, identify vulnerabilities that execute at runtime, and block malicious functions with high precision.  
According to the company, its platform can also prevent supply chain attacks, while providing organizations with zero-day response and larger patching windows through virtual patching.  
Oligo will use the fresh funding to accelerate product innovation and expand its global go-to-market operations.  
“Runtime is where the business lives. It’s where revenue is generated, customers interact with applications, and brand reputation is won or lost,” said Ballistic Ventures partner Jake Seid.
“Oligo has solved one of security’s hardest problems by protecting production environments without forcing organizations to choose between security and uptime. Their combination of technical innovation, customer momentum, and category leadership made our decision to increase our investment an easy one,” Seid added.

results.name: Oligo raises $60M to expand runtime security for cloud, AI
results.content:
# Oligo raises $60M to expand runtime security  
Oligo Security raised $60 million, bringing total funding to $140 million. The Tel Aviv company will use the capital to speed product development and expand global sales and support.  
Oligo Security announced a $60 million funding round that brings the Tel Aviv firm’s total capital to $140 million. Investors in the round include Ballistic Ventures, Canon Capital, Greenfield Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Red Dot Capital, TLV Partners and a group of angel backers. Founded in 2022, Oligo builds a runtime security platform for application code, cloud workloads and AI systems.  
The company’s platform monitors code as it runs and uses execution-level visibility to detect and block exploit attempts in production environments. Oligo describes functions that identify which vulnerabilities are actively risky in live systems, automate incident responses and block malicious behavior with high precision. The product offers virtual patching to extend the time available to apply fixes and provides a stated capability for zero-day response and mitigation of supply chain threats.
Oligo says the interval between vulnerability disclosure and active exploitation has narrowed, particularly with wider use of AI systems, and that protecting the runtime layer can catch attacks that bypass earlier defenses. The firm focuses on stopping exploits at the application layer and surfacing vulnerabilities that only appear when code executes in production.  
Jake Seid, a partner at Ballistic Ventures, described runtime as “where the business lives. It’s where revenue is generated, customers interact with applications, and brand reputation is won or lost.” He added that Oligo protects production environments without forcing organizations to choose between security and uptime, and that the company’s technical progress and customer momentum influenced Ballistic’s decision to increase its investment.  
Oligo plans to use the funding to accelerate product development and to grow sales and support operations internationally. The company has targeted cloud-native and AI-driven applications, where rapid deployment cycles and complex third-party dependencies can make traditional patching and testing slower to respond to active threats.

results.name: Oligo Security raises $60 million to expand runtime protection as AI speeds up exploit development
results.content:
Runtime security startup Oligo Security has raised $60 million in new funding to accelerate product innovation and expand global go-to-market operations. The round, announced today, comes as attackers increasingly use AI to find vulnerabilities and build exploits at machine speed, making runtime protection a critical line of defense for production systems.
### How Oligo's runtime approach works  
Oligo's software sits alongside applications in production. A sensor built on [eBPF](https://ebpf.io/?ref=completeaitraining.com), the Linux kernel feature, tracks which library functions a workload actually calls. Most vulnerabilities flagged by scanners are never called at all, and Oligo tells customers they can leave those alone. The ones that do get called can be blocked mid-exploit at the application layer, without killing the container or the process behind it.  
That last capability arrived in April with Runtime Exploit Blocking, which defends against classes of attack techniques rather than individual CVEs. A single rule can cover zero-day and n-day exploits that share a pattern. Oligo also pitches the approach as a way to buy time through virtual patching between patch cycles.  
Interest in runtime defenses has climbed since unauthorized access to Anthropic's restricted Claude Mythos model sharpened concern about how quickly vulnerability discovery and exploit development can be automated.
### Growth, partnerships, and funding details  
Oligo put annual recurring revenue growth at 300% for the past year. Valuation has more than doubled since Greenfield Partners led a $50 million Series B in January 2025, though the company gave no dollar figure for either.  
In February, AWS named Oligo as the exclusive AI runtime security partner for the extended plan of AWS Security Hub. In June, Oligo joined Palantir's FedStart program to speed its path to FedRAMP High and Department of Defense Impact Level 5 authorization - a prerequisite for selling into federal agencies and defense customers.  
Brad Arkin, a cybersecurity adviser and former chief trust officer at Salesforce, said in the announcement that runtime is "the one place where security teams can accurately determine what's truly exploitable."  
Backing the round were Ballistic Ventures, Canon Capital, Greenfield Partners, Lightspeed Management, Red Dot Capital Partners and TLV Partners, along with investor Eyal Waldman, who co-founded Mellanox Technologies. Oligo first surfaced publicly in February 2023 with $28 million from Lightspeed, Ballistic and TLV. The company puts its funding to date at $140 million.

results.name: OLIGO Security raises $60m to counter AI-speed attacks
results.content:
[OLIGO Security](https://www.oligo.security/), the runtime security company, has raised $60m in fresh funding as it races to help organisations keep pace with attacks that are now being planned and executed by AI at machine speed.  
The round takes OLIGO’s total funding to $140m and drew backing from Ballistic Ventures, Canon Capital, Greenfield Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Red Dot Capital Partners and TLV Partners, alongside angel investors including Eyal Waldman, the co-founder of Mellanox Technologies, which NVIDIA acquired for $6.9bn.  
The company said the raise caps a strong year of growth, with revenue climbing 300% year-on-year and its valuation more than doubling since its Series B.  
Over the same period, OLIGO was named by AWS as its exclusive AI runtime security partner for AWS Security Hub Extended, and it joined Palantir’s FedStart Programme to speed up its route to FedRAMP High and DoD Impact Level 5 authorisation. The firm also launched Runtime Exploit Blocking, a capability that detects and stops exploit attempts at the application layer as they happen.  
OLIGO plans to put the new capital towards product development and expanding its go-to-market operations internationally, as it works towards its goal of helping businesses block zero-day and n-day exploits before they cause damage.
The company provides runtime security for applications, cloud workloads and AI systems, pairing continuous visibility into live code execution with real-time protection. This lets customers intercept exploit attempts without disrupting production systems, filter out unnecessary vulnerability alerts and gain breathing room between patch releases through virtual patching.  
The rise in enterprise adoption of OLIGO’s platform, together with the milestones reached over the past year, points to a broader shift in how the market is responding to AI-enabled threats, with runtime protection increasingly viewed as essential rather than optional.  
OLIGO Security co-founder and CEO Nadav Czerninski said, “AI has fundamentally changed the economics of exploitation. When attackers can find vulnerabilities and build exploits at machine speed, runtime becomes the only place you can definitively understand true risk and stop attacks without impacting production. Our investors have seen this transition firsthand through the outcomes we drive for customers, and they’re doubling down because they know runtime will define the next era of cybersecurity.”
